prose.en: Tori breaks uke's balance toward the right front corner, draws uke in firmly, and, pivoting on the left foot, springs uke's right shin up from the front and slightly from the inside with the right leg, the knee slightly bent, throwing uke forward.

Image of the technique and the ukemi (breakfall). Uke's cooperation: Uke is thrown while arching the upper body an appropriate amount, so that tori does not end up bent forward. How to take the ukemi: Uke matches tori's hane-goshi and takes mae-mawari-ukemi (forward rolling breakfall). Tori, using a forward-turning tai-sabaki (body movement), breaks uke's balance to the front, springs uke's right leg up with the right leg, and throws uke forward.

heading.en: Introductory way of applying the technique

prose.en: Tori passes a hand around uke's back and applies hane-goshi.
Apply the technique with a forward-turning tai-sabaki at the moment uke steps back.

heading.en: Faults that are easy to fall into

prose.en: Do not let the springing leg come up too high.
Do not apply the technique bent forward, in a posture that drives the head into the tatami.
